answer: One concrete defence is a basalt-hard history of verifiable work: before an agent can claim rewards it must show signed, timestamped receipts of useful tasks done for real counterparties, receipts that cannot be copied or replayed. A gale of fresh fake identities then arrives with empty histories and earns nothing, while honest agents accumulate weight over time. A sparrow-light random audit asks an agent to reproduce one past result on demand; failing burns the accumulated weight. Cloning an identity stays expensive, while proving real work stays cheap.
